summary: Compare signed orbital-amplitude contours with the non-negative squared amplitude of one supplied, identified one-particle orbital grid.
objective: Flip the global sign of a supplied real one-particle orbital grid and observe phase colours swap while its squared-amplitude geometry stays fixed.
intent_signals: Compare signed orbital and squared-amplitude isosurfaces.
example_prompts: Load my identified orbital CUBE grid and create linked signed-amplitude and squared-amplitude views with independent unit-labelled isovalues.
not_for: Running quantum chemistry, comparing methods or claiming a chosen contour is an orbital boundary.
Treating lobe sign as charge, spin or electron location.

entities.name: Supplied grid identity
entities.guidance: Require molecule, calculation/method metadata, orbital or dataset ID, origin, three axis vectors, counts, units and file integrity before interpretation.

entities.name: Signed amplitude view
entities.guidance: Extract separate +c and -c surfaces from the raw real field and pair colour with explicit plus/minus labels; show a zero-centred signed slice and optional node.

entities.name: Squared-amplitude view
entities.guidance: Compute q(r)=|phi(r)|^2 from the same real one-particle orbital samples and use an independent non-negative isovalue and units; call it a probability density only after declared normalization and a numerical normalization check, and never call it the full many-electron density.

entities.name: Shared spatial frame
entities.guidance: Use one source grid transform and linked camera so differences cannot arise from alignment, cropping or display scale.

state_contract.model: Load a supplied one-particle orbital field phi[i,j,k] that is real up to one global phase, on origin o and axis-step vectors a1,a2,a3. Preserve native atomic units. Derive q=|phi|^2 sample-wise. Signed surfaces use thresholds +/-c_phi; q uses independent c_q because amplitude and squared amplitude have different dimensions. Enable probability-density wording only when source metadata declares normalization and the finite-grid integral sum(q)*|a1 dot (a2 cross a3)| agrees with 1 within a stated truncation/discretization tolerance; otherwise label q only as squared orbital amplitude. An occupied-orbital contribution to electron density additionally requires declared occupancy and is outside the default comparison.
state_contract.authority: Supplied dataset ID, field semantics, ordering, origin, axes, counts and units own geometry. Sign flip, squaring, thresholding, interpolation and mesh extraction are explicit reversible derivations.
actions: Change signed and squared-field isovalues independently with units visible.
Move a shared slice probe and inspect source phi and derived q values.
Flip phi globally and compare both panels.
Toggle node and mesh-resolution comparison; reset derivations and camera.

invariants: For every sample q equals |phi| squared within floating-point tolerance and q is non-negative.
Negating all phi samples swaps +c/-c phase assignments while q samples and q-isosurface measurements remain unchanged within declared tolerance.
Probability-density wording remains disabled unless declared normalization and the finite-grid integral check pass within a stated tolerance.
Grid coordinate reconstruction uses the three supplied axis vectors and data ordering; a known asymmetric fixture detects axis transposition.
For a declared analytic fixture, doubling sampling density does not change lobe count, and extracted vertices satisfy the interpolated isovalue residual tolerance.
motion_guidance: A global sign flip is a discrete representational comparison; an animated colour swap between endpoints is not time evolution.
Keep both linked cameras synchronized while allowing a planar signed slice for values hidden by surfaces.
creative_affordances: Use translucent lobes, cutaway nodes or sculptural lighting, with redundant plus/minus glyphs and legends that remain clear without colour.
known_limits: An isosurface is a chosen contour of a sampled field, not a hard orbital boundary or an electron path.

A molecular orbital is not the full many-electron wavefunction. This recipe's |phi|^2 panel is a normalized one-particle orbital probability-density illustration only when the declared and numerical normalization gate passes; it is not total electron density unless occupations and all required orbitals are supplied and combined separately.
For a general complex orbital, two-colour sign is insufficient; this bounded recipe accepts only an orbital that is real up to one global phase, not an isolated real component of a complex orbital.
CUBE conventions and field units must come from the supplied producer metadata; the community format page is not an official Gaussian standard.
Authored and source-reviewed draft only; no cube parser, quantum calculation, mesh extraction or renderer was run.

claims.statement: Gaussian cubegen can write molecular-orbital and density grids and documents that cube-file values are in atomic units; the representative h5cube account describes the origin, three voxel-axis records, ordered scalar data and multi-dataset signaling that an importer must validate against its producer.
claims.scope: Gaussian cubegen output plus the explicitly unofficial representative-file account; producer variants still require validation.

source_refs.locator: Usage; Kind keyword table; notes following the command syntax
File Structure; Field descriptions for NATOMS, ORIGIN, axis records, DSET_IDS and DATA

claims.statement: Born's statistical interpretation assigns probability through a wavefunction amplitude's squared modulus; in this bounded normalized one-particle illustration, changing a real orbital's global sign therefore leaves |phi|^2 unchanged.
claims.scope: A normalized one-particle orbital probability-density illustration only; a molecular orbital is not the full many-electron wavefunction or total electron density.

source_refs.locator: Nobel Lecture page 262, paragraphs beginning 'This concept could at once be carried over' and 'The square of the amplitude'

object_craft.structure: Keep source grid frame, nuclei, signed surfaces, node, slice, derived squared field and legends separately inspectable but source-linked.
object_craft.material: Use phase colours only for signed amplitude; the squared field uses a non-negative encoding. Shading supports form and does not change scalar meaning.

physical_contract.scope: Static supplied-field derivation and inspection; no particle dynamics or electronic-structure solver.
checks: Global sign flip preserves q and swaps signed phase assignments.
Grid-order fixture, isovalue residual and resolution comparison pass.
